definitions.explanation: A characteristic Japanese flavor profile combining sweetness (often from sugar or mirin) with the savory saltiness of soy sauce. Typical of teriyaki, simmered dishes, and many sauces — not "sweet and spicy" despite the literal kanji.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{味|あじ}→味：00826_aji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{甘辛|あまから}い。
{甘辛|あまから}い⟦タレ→タレ：10500_tare⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦かけた→かける：00854_kakeru⟧。
examples.english: I poured the sweet-and-savory sauce over the meat.

examples.japanese: {甘辛|あまから}い⟦{味付|あじつ}け→味付け：05830_ajitsuke⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{白|しろ}→白：13854_shiro⟧⟦ご{飯|はん}→ご飯：00776_gohan⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{相性|あいしょう}→相性：13654_aishou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{抜群|ばつぐん}→抜群：12783_batsugun⟧だ。
examples.english: A sweet-and-savory seasoning goes exceptionally well with plain rice.

notes:
Despite containing ⟦{辛|から}い→辛い：00638_karai⟧ (spicy/salty), this word almost always refers to the soy-sauce-and-sugar flavor of Japanese home cooking, not chili heat. Think teriyaki, sukiyaki broth, or simmered fish.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甘辛|あまから}い⟦タレ→タレ：10500_tare⟧: sweet-and-savory sauce
- {甘辛|あまから}い⟦{味付|あじつ}け→味付け：05830_ajitsuke⟧: sweet-and-savory seasoning
- {甘辛|あまから}い⟦{煮物|にもの}→煮物：04971_nimono⟧: sweet-and-savory simmered dish

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {甘辛|あまから}: the noun form, used in compounds like {甘辛|あまから}{煮|に} (sweet-savory simmered dish)
- ⟦{甘酸|あまず}っぱい→甘酸っぱい：05916_amazuppai⟧: sweet and sour — fruity tartness; very different flavor
- ⟦{辛|から}い→辛い：00638_karai⟧: salty; spicy — covers both "hot" and "salty" in Japanese, but context usually makes it clear
